title: Vitruvyan Motus trace document, v1
description: v1 — accepted by ADR-001 on 2026-08-03. A trace is a run header plus an ordered append-only sequence of records: the causal, replayable account of one GRAPH EXECUTION — not merely a well-formed record sequence. Two canonical encodings of ONE logical model: (a) a single JSON document matching this schema's root; (b) JSONL — UTF-8, LF line endings ONLY (a validator REJECTS CR bytes anywhere in the stream, rule JSONL3 — canonical writers emit LF and readers do not silently normalize), no BOM, exactly one header line matching #/$defs/TraceHeader followed by one line per record matching #/$defs/Record; blank lines are tolerated and ignored (a crash may leave a trailing empty line). A JSON document and a JSONL stream are equivalent iff header (minus records) and record sequences are structurally equal; fixtures pin this. Integrity hashes, when a future revision activates them, are computed over the canonical object form (contract/README.md), never over encoding bytes; in every version accepted here they are typed null. A conformant validator MUST enforce, beyond this schema (executable in contract/validate.py): — THE T-RULES (record coherence): (T1) seq monotonic and gapless from 1; (T2) run_started appears exactly once, as the first record; (T3) the last record of a finished run is run_completed | run_failed | run_cancelled, and nothing follows a terminal record; a stream ending without one is incomplete/crash-truncated per guarantees.md invariant II; (T4) every read origin resolves to the exact value it names: kind transition references an EARLIER transition whose writes[collection][index] EXISTS AND WHOSE KEY EQUALS the read's key (for facts/decisions); kind initial likewise into run_started.initial_state; kind scan requires read.key == origin.collection; kind header field intent requires read.key == 'intent', field metadata requires the key to exist in run.metadata (a missing key is an absent read); kind absent carries the surface that missed (facts | decisions | metadata); (T5) node, after, selected, candidates[].target, active_attempt.node and run_failed.failed_node name declared nodes, or the literal END where permitted; (T6) every transition (node, attempt) is opened by the immediately preceding attempt_started with the same pair; an unclosed attempt_started may be followed only by run_cancelled naming it, run_failed with a non-node cause, or EOF (incomplete); conversely run_cancelled.active_attempt, when non-null, names exactly the immediately preceding unclosed attempt_started, else it is null; (T7) run_failed.failed_node is non-null iff cause.kind is node_failure, and cause.record_seq, when non-null, references an existing record; (T8) routing correlations: matched has exactly one taken candidate with condition {kind map, key == value} and target == selected; default has exactly one taken candidate with condition kind default (and, spec available, value absent from the map keys); static has exactly one candidate, taken, kind static, target == selected; miss has zero taken and selected END; the candidate list is the complete route step (every map entry once, default once when declared, or the single static edge); EVERY routed outcome — matched, default AND miss — carries the same causal duty through `origin`, which addresses the exact Decision observed: kind transition names an EARLIER committed transition's writes.decisions[index], kind initial names run_started.initial_state.decisions[index], and both must carry key `on` and a value EQUAL to the routed value under JSON equality (type-aware: the boolean true is not the number 1); kind absent asserts that no decision with key `on` exists anywhere in the run — seeded or committed — and is admissible only on a miss, only with value null, because nothing observed may be reported as something; R10 staleness holds for transition and initial origins alike, in BOTH directions recency runs: no LATER committed decision with that key before this routing, and no later entry with that key inside the origin's OWN array — R10 says last-in-array, so an earlier index is stale even when the later entry carries an identical value, because the origin promises the exact Decision observed and not an equivalent payload; origin is null exactly for a static step; and a miss must have been POSSIBLE — with a spec, a STRING value that is a declared map key was matched, and an unmapped STRING on a route declaring a default was defaulted (R7), so neither may be recorded as a miss, while a NON-STRING value is always a miss under R9 whether or not a default is declared, since it is never coerced; (T9) every ts and created_ts is a calendar-valid RFC 3339 UTC instant; (T10) replay capability only degrades: the terminal record's capability is equal to or weaker than the header's declared one (full > partial > none), and no constraint present in the declaration is absent from the final status — a run may discover it is less reproducible than it hoped, never more; (T11) THE INTEGRITY CHAIN: each record's integrity.payload_hash is sha256 over the canonical object form of that record WITHOUT its own integrity block — a hash cannot cover itself — and prev_hash is the preceding record's payload_hash, null on the first record, which has no predecessor. The SCHEMA VERSION IS THE ACTIVATION INDICATOR and there is deliberately no second flag: 2.0.0 REQUIRES the chain and a validator RECOMPUTES it, 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 REQUIRE both fields null so an unverified hash cannot ride in an old trace and pass for tamper evidence. Checking the chain's shape alone proves nothing — an editor who alters a record can recompute a well-formed hash; what they cannot do is reproduce the root that was anchored outside their reach. A trace therefore carries its own chain and is re-checkable from nothing but itself, and its ROOT is the terminal record's payload_hash, derived and never stored twice; (T12) interaction_fingerprint and fingerprint_salt travel together or not at all, and only in 2.0.0 — the digest is meaningless without the salt that prefixed its material, and a salt alone describes nothing. Neither is RECOMPUTABLE by a validator: the covered material is deliberately not in the trace, which is the point of the field, so a clean validation NEVER means the fingerprint was checked. What is enforceable is that the pair is complete, and publishing which half is enforced is the difference between a narrow guarantee and a misleading one; (J1) values are strict RFC 8259, checked RECURSIVELY at every depth on the API path: non-finite numbers, non-string mapping keys, tuples and any non-JSON Python object are refused — and refused by the CLI parser for NaN/Infinity literals. — THE E-RULES (the execution state machine binding the trace to graph semantics; 'cancel/system-failure' below means: run_cancelled per T6, or run_failed with cause in {sink_failure, validation_failure, runner_internal}): (E1) the record after run_started is attempt_started(entry, 1), or cancel/system-failure — a run never completes without executing entry; (E2) after transition(returned, commit): routing(after = that node), or cancel/system-failure; (E3) after transition(raised, retry): attempt_started(same node, attempt + 1), or cancel/system-failure; (E4) after transition(raised, abort): run_failed(node_failure, failed_node = that node, record_seq = that transition's seq); (E5) transition(raised, continue) requires policy exploration, followed by routing(after = same node), or cancel/system-failure; (E6) after transition(cancelled, abort): run_cancelled with active_attempt null (the attempt closed itself cooperatively); (E7) after routing with outcome matched/default/static selecting node X: attempt_started(X, 1), or run_failed(transition_limit_exceeded, record_seq = that routing's seq), or cancel/system-failure; (E8) after routing selecting END with outcome matched/default/static: run_completed, or cancel/system-failure; (E9) after routing outcome miss: policy strict — run_failed(route_miss, record_seq = that routing's seq); policy exploration — run_completed (the miss is on record); or cancel/system-failure; (E10) attempt numbering: 1 at each routing-driven activation of a node, incremented only by E3 retries within the activation; (E11) admissibility of failure causes: node_failure only per E4; route_miss only per E9-strict; transition_limit_exceeded only per E7, and (spec available) only when the spec declares max_transitions and routing-producing activations reached it (returned/commit and raised/continue transitions count; retry attempts do not). — THE SB-RULES (spec binding, when validate_trace receives a GraphSpec): (SB1) run.graph.name, .version and .spec_schema_version equal the supplied spec's; (SB2) run.graph.graph_fingerprint equals the fingerprint RECOMPUTED over the supplied spec's canonical form per contract/README.md — a trace cannot claim one graph and be checked against another; code_fingerprint is NOT offline-verifiable without the runtime's node registry, an explicit limitation; (SB3) every transition's effect_class equals the spec node's declared class, or external_effect when undeclared; (SB4) each transition's violations list is TRUTHFUL: recomputed from the spec's reads_declared/writes_declared against EVERY captured read — no origin kind is exempt: an absent read is captured because a miss steers control flow, a scan read's key is the collection it swept, a header read's key is `intent` or the metadata key taken — and against every fact/decision write key, and must match exactly, no missing and no invented violations.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS trace schema. Single-sourced in the package; a contract test asserts equality.

TraceHeader.description: Line 1 of the JSONL encoding: this document minus records — so both encodings name the schema version that produced them.

run_id.description: Exposed as `.trace_id` on the legacy compatibility view (guarantees.md §4).

durability_profile.description: Which crash guarantee this run bought. See guarantees.md invariant II.

sink.description: Sink configuration disclosing the delivery window. Validator rule H1: when durability_profile is `buffered`, `sink` MUST be present WITH BOTH disclosure keys (flush_interval_ms and chunk_records) — an empty sink object discloses nothing and does not satisfy the rule. Optional otherwise. When a caller explicitly supplies a sink under `in-memory` or `synchronous`, the runtime records its effective synchronous delivery as flush_interval_ms 0 and chunk_records 1; this disclosure does not strengthen the profile's crash guarantee.

replay.description: The capability DECLARED at run start. The FINAL capability — after any mid-run downgrade (node-protocol.md §6.2) — is on the terminal record; when both exist, the terminal record is authoritative.

metadata.description: Run provenance. Open map; the keys below are the standard, tooling-expected vocabulary. Consumers MAY add their own keys (Terraveler's carta_version maps onto ruleset_version). Metadata VALUES are #/$defs/Value: redaction is representable here, and a hand-forged partial {kind: redacted} object is invalid exactly as in any other value position.

actor.description: Whose authority the run acts under.

causation_id.description: The event that woke this run.

correlation_id.description: The broader request this run belongs to.

ruleset_version.description: Which consumer-defined ruleset/constitution was in force. Domain-neutral name; what a consumer calls it (carta, policy, charter) is its business.

resume.description: Motus 0.6 resume provenance. A resumed segment is a new run linked to immutable prior evidence.

capability.description: Explicit, recorded property. Absence of a declaration never implies reproducibility; a run that did not declare it is `none`.

constraints.description: Machine-readable reasons for a non-full capability, e.g. 'node:fetch_page:ambient_time' or the standard reason 'undeclared'.

ReplayStatus.description: full carries no constraints; partial/none carry at least one motivating constraint ('undeclared' is the standard reason for runs that never declared reproducibility).

ts.description: From the run clock — never from ambient wall time (invariant IV.1).

payload_hash.description: The record's own digest: sha256 over the canonical object form of this record WITHOUT its integrity block — a hash cannot cover itself — never over encoding bytes, so a document and a JSONL stream of one trace hash identically. Null is admitted here ONLY so a 1.x trace still validates; rule T11 requires it non-null in 2.0.0 and null below, which is the activation indicator: the schema version IS the claim, and there is no second flag that could disagree with it. Earlier wording promised activation "in 1.1+" while typing the property null unconditionally, so 1.1 announced a capability its own types forbade.

prev_hash.description: The preceding record's payload_hash, or null for the first record, which has no predecessor — a genesis constant would look like evidence and carry none. Altering any record breaks its own digest and every prev_hash after it, which is what makes a trace re-checkable from nothing but itself. See payload_hash and rule T11.

intent.description: The run's declared intent, if any. A PLAIN-TEXT surface, deliberately not redactable (cross-review MF2-06, narrowed by decision): intent, error messages, effect descriptions and reason fields identify and explain — they MUST NOT carry secret content (node-protocol.md §5.3); sensitive material rides in Value positions, which support redaction. Readable by nodes; reads resolve as origin {kind: header, field: intent}.

initial_state.description: Snapshot of everything present before the first transition (all arrays may be empty). Reads with origin kind `initial` address into these arrays by collection and index — a seeded run is replayable and why-value-answerable for its seed.

AttemptStarted.description: Opens every attempt, before the node is invoked (T6). This is what makes a cancellation or crash mid-node EVIDENT instead of absent: an unclosed attempt_started names the node that was in flight, and effects it may or may not have caused are declared unknown — not erased from history.

allOf.description: Effect lattice: a recorded_effect node may describe recorded effects only. pure describes none (the conditional above). external_effect is the only class permitted to describe both — a node that mutates the world may also read it.

node.description: Node name as declared in the GraphSpec (T5).

attempt.description: Matches the opening attempt_started (T6). Every attempt gets its own attempt_started + transition pair — retries are never hidden.

outcome.description: What the ATTEMPT did: returned a state, raised, or was cancelled cooperatively mid-checkpoint. Distinct from disposition — what the RUNNER then did about it.

disposition.description: The runner's policy decision: commit the returned state; retry the node (a new attempt_started follows); abort the run (run_failed follows, under strict); continue past the failure (exploration). Correlations are enforced by schema conditionals: returned→commit; raised→retry|abort|continue; cancelled→abort.

effect_class.description: The node's resolved class (declared in the GraphSpec or defaulted to external_effect). Recorded here so the trace document is self-sufficient for replay-mode selection. pure implies an empty effects list (schema-enforced). The node's class BOUNDS its descriptors (effect lattice, schema-enforced): pure describes no effects; recorded_effect describes recorded effects only; external_effect may describe either. A descriptor cannot exceed the class its node declared.

key.description: The logical key read (fact/decision key, metadata key, or the collection name for scans). Captured, not declared.

reads.description: Every read the node actually performed, each with the structured origin of the exact value read — collection and index, not just a transition. Absent reads are captured too: reading a missing key can steer control flow as much as a present value.

effects.description: Per-effect evidence (node-protocol.md §4). Schema 1.1 adds adapter-supplied receipts for Motus 0.6 replay and resume. For raised/cancelled attempts this list is best-effort: effects the runtime observed before the interruption.

context_draws.description: Every RunContext draw this attempt made, in draw order. Empty for nodes that drew nothing.

violations.description: Declared-vs-captured mismatches (node-protocol.md §3.2). Motus 0.6 fails strict attempts before commit and records the captured violation; exploration records and continues.

error.description: Null iff outcome is returned or cancelled; the raising error otherwise (schema-enforced).

Writes.description: Everything this attempt appended. Transactional rule (node-protocol.md §7): writes exist only when the node returned and the runner committed — an attempt that raised or was cancelled has, by the state→state protocol, handed nothing to the runner, so its writes are structurally empty. What such a node did internally before raising never reached the run.

oneOf.description: The value read is records[seq].writes[collection][index] (T4). Collection + index make the edge per-VALUE: two same-key writes in one transition, or a fact and a decision sharing a key, resolve unambiguously.
The value read is the run's intent, or the metadata entry named by the read's key.

The node read the collection as a whole (iteration, len, search) rather than one addressed value. The read's key is the collection name. Coarse by nature: a scan depends on everything in the collection at that point.

surface.description: Which readable namespace missed. Facts, decisions and metadata are distinct surfaces that may share a key — an absent read without its surface is ambiguous evidence.

oneOf.description: The key was looked up on the named surface and not found. A read-miss is causal evidence — it can steer control flow — so it is recorded with its surface, never dropped.

after.description: The node whose committed transition triggered this routing (T5).

on.description: The decision key routed on; null exactly for static steps (schema-enforced by outcome conditionals).

value.description: The observed decision value (Value admits JSON null — no duplicate null branch, per cross-review MF-02). String for matched/default (graphspec R9); anything, including null when the key was never decided, for miss; null for static (schema-enforced by the outcome conditionals).

outcome.description: matched: value hit a map key. default: value missed the map and the declared default was taken. miss: strict route missed (graphspec R7) — selected is END; the run then fails under policy strict and ends with the miss on record under exploration. static: a next/terminal step, no dispatch.

selected.description: A declared node name, or the literal string END.

condition.description: WHY this route was a candidate: the map key it answers to, the declared default, or the static next/terminal edge. Two map entries pointing at one target stay distinguishable.

candidates.description: Every route possible at this point — all map entries exactly once, the default once when declared, or the single static edge — taken and not taken (T8). This is what why-not answers are made of.

origin.description: The routing record's own causal edge (T8): the Decision this dispatch observed, addressed exactly. Null only for a static step, where no dispatch happened.

replay.description: FINAL replay capability after any mid-run downgrade. Authoritative over the header's declared value.

record_seq.description: The record that evidences the cause (the failing transition, the miss routing record), when one exists (T7).

cause.description: Structured cause so failure is explainable without parsing messages: a node raised, a strict route missed, the required sink refused the trace, a value failed boundary validation, the max_transitions safety limit tripped (transition_limit_exceeded), or the runner itself failed. PERSISTENCE LIMITATION (cross-review, OPEN-08): when the cause is sink_failure, THIS record's own persistence through the failed sink is best-effort — the run's logical failure toward the caller is still guaranteed (invariant II), but the persisted trace may end crash-truncated exactly as its durability profile describes. The contract cannot promise to write the death certificate into the register that just burned; it promises the death is declared.

failed_node.description: Non-null iff cause.kind is node_failure (T7). The accumulated trace up to and including this record survives — failure preservation is invariant-level.

replay.description: FINAL replay capability. Authoritative over the header's declared value.

reason.description: Cancellation is a first-class, trace-recorded runner outcome — never a silently abandoned generator.

active_attempt.description: The attempt in flight when cancellation landed, or null if cancellation fell between nodes. T6 binds BOTH directions: non-null active_attempt names exactly the immediately preceding UNCLOSED attempt_started; when the preceding record is not an unclosed attempt_started, active_attempt MUST be null — it can neither invent an attempt nor resurrect a closed one. Whether the in-flight attempt's external effects happened is UNKNOWN and recorded as such by this structure — the evidence is preserved, not erased.

replay.description: FINAL replay capability. Authoritative over the header's declared value.

ErrorInfo.description: Plain-text surfaces (see run_started.intent): error type and message explain, they are not redactable and MUST NOT carry secret content.

source.description: Free-form provenance label supplied by the node. The kernel records it and never interprets it.

Fact.description: A RECORDED ASSERTION by a node — evidence of what was asserted, by whom, from what claimed source, at what point in the run. Never a claim of truth, verification, or endorsement: Fact/Decision/Rejection are neutral workflow primitives (guarantees.md invariant III note), and attributing truth to them is the consumer's business.

Decision.description: The Motus-native decision: a keyed, routable value with an optional reason. Distinct from the legacy Axis Decision(description, timestamp), which never enters a v1 trace — see guarantees.md §4 for the compatibility strategy.

Rejection.description: A recorded not-taken: what was declined and why. `evidence` is optional; when present it is a Value (which itself admits JSON null).

class.description: The class of THIS effect. `pure` is a node-level classification (Transition.effect_class), not an effect — a pure effect is an oxymoron and does not validate.

idempotency_key.description: A non-empty key plus a completed receipt is required before Motus 0.6 will resume past an observed external effect.

result_fingerprint.description: Adapter-supplied fingerprint of the effect's result, and a 1.x field only. Its FORMAT is fixed here and its SUBJECT is not: no recipe defines what it is taken of, so two producers with the same result may stamp different values, and validate.py does not recompute it. Unverifiable, like receipt_id. Schema 2.0.0 supersedes it with interaction_fingerprint, named for what ADR-014 decided it covers; this field is NOT redefined in place, because a 1.x value means what 1.x said it meant, forever.

interaction_fingerprint.description: Schema 2.0.0. Adapter-supplied digest binding WHAT WAS ASKED of the external system to WHAT CAME BACK, as one value (ADR-014). Fingerprinting the result alone leaves the request swappable underneath an unchanged answer, which in an advisory setting is how a recorded interaction is actually disputed: not "you never said that" but "that is not what I asked". Computed over the canonical object form of the pair, prefixed by fingerprint_salt, using the same canonicalisation as graph_fingerprint — a second rule would be a second thing that can disagree with the first. Its purpose is TAMPER EVIDENCE, not cross-producer comparison: it establishes that an archived interaction is the one this run produced, which is the binding between a trace and material deliberately held elsewhere. validate.py CANNOT recompute it — the covered material is not in the trace — so its guarantee is narrower than "the validator checks it" and stronger than "unverifiable": verifiable by a party holding the trace AND the archive together. A clean validation never means this field was checked.

fingerprint_salt.description: Schema 2.0.0. The per-effect random salt prefixing the material interaction_fingerprint covers. Required whenever that field is present and absent without it (rule T12). Recorded, therefore public, and it must be described for what it does: it gives domain separation — two runs holding the same interaction produce different digests, so an archive cannot be correlated across runs by comparing fingerprints — and it defeats precomputation, because a table built once against likely inputs is worthless when every effect carries its own salt. It does NOT confer confidentiality on a guessable input: a holder of the trace has the digest and the salt together. What makes that acceptable is the SUBJECT and not the salt — the digest covers request and result bound together, and a free-text result is not guessable. A deployment whose request and result are BOTH low-entropy needs a keyed digest and must choose it knowingly.

interaction_fingerprint.description: Schema 2.0.0. Adapter-supplied digest binding WHAT WAS ASKED of the external system to WHAT CAME BACK, as one value (ADR-014). Fingerprinting the result alone leaves the request swappable underneath an unchanged answer, which in an advisory setting is how a recorded interaction is actually disputed: not "you never said that" but "that is not what I asked". Computed over the canonical object form of the pair, prefixed by fingerprint_salt, using the same canonicalisation as graph_fingerprint — a second rule would be a second thing that can disagree with the first. Its purpose is TAMPER EVIDENCE, not cross-producer comparison: it establishes that an archived interaction is the one this run produced, which is the binding between a trace and material deliberately held elsewhere. validate.py CANNOT recompute it — the covered material is not in the trace — so its guarantee is narrower than "the validator checks it" and stronger than "unverifiable": verifiable by a party holding the trace AND the archive together. A clean validation never means this field was checked.

fingerprint_salt.description: Schema 2.0.0. The per-effect random salt that prefixes the material interaction_fingerprint covers. REQUIRED whenever that field is present, and absent without it. Recorded, therefore public, and it must be described for what it does: it gives domain separation — two runs holding the same interaction produce different digests, so an archive cannot be correlated across runs by comparing fingerprints — and it defeats precomputation, because a table built once against likely inputs is worthless when every effect carries its own salt. It does NOT confer confidentiality on a guessable input: a holder of the trace has the digest and the salt together. What makes that acceptable is the SUBJECT, not the salt — the digest covers request and result bound together, and a free-text result is not guessable. A deployment whose request and result are BOTH low-entropy needs a keyed digest and must choose it knowingly.

EffectReceipt.description: Adapter-supplied effect evidence. Recorded by Motus, never upgraded into an exactly-once claim.

oneOf.description: Any RFC 8259 JSON value EXCEPT an object claiming the reserved top-level discriminator kind: 'redacted' — such an object must be a well-formed RedactedValue or it is invalid everywhere. This keeps redacted values reserved and runtime-produced within a trace (they are not cryptographically unforgeable; a trace received from outside is only as trustworthy as its provenance until integrity activates in 1.1).

RedactedValue.description: Invariant V: structural completeness without content exposure. The hash and policy reference are evidence; the secret is not. Produced only by the runtime's redaction API (node-protocol.md §5).

Json.description: An RFC 8259 JSON value, strictly: object keys are strings; NaN and Infinity are refused at the write boundary (Python's json module accepts them by default — Motus does not); values round-trip structurally. A value that cannot be written down under these rules is a contract violation at the boundary, not a silent pass-through.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC with the literal Z suffix — the single canonical emission (readers MAY accept +00:00 in legacy inputs; writers emit Z only). From the run clock (invariant IV.1).

Fingerprint.description: Kind-prefixed SHA-256 over canonical form. See contract/README.md.

oneOf.description: The routed value is records[seq].writes.decisions[index], committed by an earlier transition.

The routed value is run_started.initial_state.decisions[index] — a seeded decision. A run resumed or seeded with decisions can route on them and say so; the scalar predecessor could not express this at all.
No decision with this key exists anywhere in the run — neither seeded nor committed. Admissible only on a miss, and only with value null: nothing was observed, so nothing may be reported.

DecisionOrigin.description: Where the routed value came from, addressed to the exact Decision (collection position), not merely to a record. Symmetric with ReadOrigin: one provenance mechanism in this schema, not two.
